comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide study BA-JAP and its public product API identify 60 EC in each year. The chosen coherent pathway selects the Leiden 15-EC second-year route (Modern Japanese 2c, 10 EC, and a second shared East Asian course, 5 EC), rather than the Japan study-abroad route; one permitted option in each seminar and restricted-choice group; the BA Thesis 10 EC plus Graduation Seminar 5 EC rather than other graduation projects; and the full 30 EC genuine third-year elective space, split into two 15-EC components. The 0-EC mentorship and non-curricular JLPT preparation are excluded. The adopted OER confirms no formal graduation tracks and the 2026–27 language progression. Course EC were checked against the public 2026–27 module entries; the study grouping and selected options account for exactly 180 EC.

exception.reason: Leiden’s 180-EC Japanese Studies pathway joins a compulsory, progressive Japanese-language sequence with Japanese history, society, material culture, literary/media seminars, Japanese-source research and a thesis. The selected pathway includes at least 70 EC of explicit Japanese language and Japanese-language practice before its research component, and several additional Japan-specific courses. UCR offers no Japanese-language course and no course whose current content addresses Japan specifically. Its general history, politics, art, literature and media courses could support a comparative or global-culture programme, but would not implement a Japan-focused 24-course academic concept or reproduce its language-based source work. A purported closest UCR Japanese Studies alternative would depend on generic disciplinary neighbours and misrepresent the core.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026–27 study BA-JAP identifies 60 EC of first-year compulsory units, a 20-EC second-year compulsory group with 40 EC of restricted choices, and a 60-EC third year comprising 15 EC of restricted specialist study, one 15-EC graduation project pathway and 30 EC of actual elective space. The BA Thesis pathway is selected. The OER confirms Japanese-language progression and primary-source competence and describes HUM and SOSCI as clusters for course choices, not formal graduation tracks. The selected external components preserve all 180 EC without counting mutually exclusive Japan stay, alternative seminars or non-curricular language preparation.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics and methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The workbook contains no Japanese, Korean, Chinese or East Asian course or language sequence. GOSHIST111/211/312 address modern history, empires and historical research without a Japan focus; GOSPOLI112/212/313 cover comparative politics, international relations and conflict without Japan-specific training. MCCHEAM111/212 and MCCLITR111/311 or MCCMEDI111/211 offer art, literature and media methods but no Japanese materials or language. Linguistic study in HCBCOGN312 is psycholinguistics, not Japanese instruction. These courses cannot make 23 non-PPD courses each contribute concretely to a Japan-centred concept, and no timetable can repair that substantive gap.
